Unit 11: Global Networking

SL curriculum overview and structured learning plan.

Introduction

How does the world stay connected?

This unit focuses on Interconnectivity and Standardisation. You will explore how heterogeneous systems communicate through common rules (Protocols) and the physical architecture required to move data globally, from local LANs to the massive WAN of the Internet.

You'll begin by defining network types (LAN, WAN, VPN) and hardware (Routers, Switches). Then you'll map out Topologies and model data flow using Packet Switching and TCP/IP. Finally, you'll secure these networks using Encryption and Firewalls.

Network Fundamentals

Networks are defined by scale and architecture:

  • LAN (Local): Small area, high speed (e.g., Home/School).
  • WAN (Wide): Large area, connects LANs (e.g., The Internet).
  • VPN (Virtual Private): A secure tunnel over a public WAN.
Packet Switching

Data doesn't travel in one big chunk. It is broken into Packets.

  • Breakdown: File sliced into packets.
  • Routing: Each packet takes the fastest route (independent paths).
  • Reassembly: Packets reordered at the destination.
Protocols (The Rules)

Computers must agree on how to talk. We use standard protocols:

  • TCP/IP: The fundamental language of the internet.
  • HTTP/HTTPS: Web pages (Secure vs plain).
  • DHCP: Assigning IP addresses automatically.
Security & Encryption

The internet is public. To keep secrets, we use math.

  • Firewall: A filter that checks incoming/outgoing packets.
  • Symmetric Encryption: Same key to lock and unlock (Fast, but how to share key?).
  • Asymmetric Encryption: Public key to lock, Private key to unlock (Secure key exchange).
Key Terminology
TermDefinition
Protocol A set of rules defining how two computers communicate (e.g., format, speed, error checking).
Bandwidth The theoretical maximum amount of data that can be transmitted over a connection in a given time.
Latency The time delay between the request for data and the receipt of the data.
Packet Switching Method of slicing data into packets, routing them individually, and reassembling them at the destination.
Router A device that forwards data packets between computer networks (typically joining a LAN to a WAN).
Switch A device that connects devices within a LAN and uses MAC addresses to filter traffic.
Encryption Encoding data so that only authorized parties can understand it.
VPN Virtual Private Network. Extends a private network across a public network allowing secure data exchange.
Topology The physical or logical arrangement of a network (e.g., Star, Mesh, Bus).
